headline: Approved a contractors site at 24 Oakhurst Road and waived site plan review at 1R Lackey Dam Road.
summary: The 24 Oakhurst Road project includes two buildings totaling 9,000 s.f., one for offices and one for contractor bays. At 1R Lackey Dam Road, the work adds a 2,580 s.f. office and 8 parking spaces for a potential tenant. The board declined to make an alternate access finding for 26R Oakhurst Road after Town Counsel said the lot does not appear to have legal frontage.
decisions: Approved a special permit, site plan, and earth disturbance permit for a contractors site at 24 Oakhurst Road, 5-0, with conditions.
Waived site plan review and allowed interior and façade renovations at 1R Lackey Dam Road, 5-0.
Declined to make the footnote 12 alternate access finding for 26R Oakhurst Road, 4-0.
Approved the minutes of 7/20/26, 4-0 with one abstention.
Named W. Stanhope chair and W. Talcott vice chair for the upcoming year, 5-0.
Appointed E. McCallum as the CMRPC delegate for the next year, 5-0.

# SUTTON PLANNING BOARD
**Meeting Minutes**
**August 03, 2026**

E. McCallum read the following notice: Pursuant to Governor Healey's directive extending the temporary Open Meeting provisions until June 30, 2027, the Planning Board meeting will be conducted in a HYBRID format and will be recorded. *Recordings will be available on the Town's website and YouTube channel. *Please be aware: Participants attending via Zoom will have their video and audio disabled. *If you wish to engage in discussion, raise your hand; if acknowledged by the Chair, you will receive a pop-up message allowing you to unmute yourself. For agenda, YouTube, and Zoom links, please visit www.suttonma.org/cable-department.

Present in person: M. Gagan, R. Largess Jr., W. Stanhope, E. McCallum, Dave Mason, Associate acting as full member

Present remotely: none

Absent: W. Talcott

Staff: J. Hager, Community Development Director

## Public Hearings

### 24 Oakhurst Road – Site Plan Review & Special Permit

Project applicants Wilson and Dianna Duarte of Silver Ledge Drive, Sutton, were present with Raouf Mankaryous, P.E. of Alpha Omega Engineering of Sutton, and Mike McGovern of 234 Manchaug Road representing McGovern Builders, Sutton. Mr. Mankaryous explained the project consists of two buildings totaling 9,000 s.f. one for offices and one for contractor bays. Mr. Duarte stated employs about 30 people. The business has about 15-20 vehicles/pieces of equipment. Most will be stored at the rear of the site with just one piece of equipment in the garage at a time for repairs. The rear two thirds of the site will be fenced with vinyl privacy fence. Hours of operation will typically be 8am to 5 pm, with most activity in the morning and evening when about half the employees come to the site, get equipment, and go to sites and conversely in the late afternoon when they return to the site before they head home. The building will likely be light gray with a stone water table on the front building featuring stone in a mix of brown/gray colors. A portion of the buildings will likely be rented to another company(s). They have requested a Special Permit for use under the Table of Use Regulations - Section G.3. for landscape contractors, arborists, and building contractors, as well as section G.8. for other contractors, not including paving. These sections cover their use as well as the types of tenants they would entertain.

R. Nunnemacher of 24 Singletary Avenue asked about the electric company easement and old roadway layout. R. Mankaryous stated the old layout will be removed and the electric easement has been extinguished and the related document has been provided.

D. Mason asked about storage of construction materials. Mr. Duarte stated none will be stored on site; they are delivered to work sites.

W. Stanhope asked about oil and water separation for the site and buildings. There will be an oil water catch basin structure as part of site drainage and a tight tank for the garage bays.

Mr. Mankaryous confirmed the septic system and well have been approved. He added there is about 400' of sight distance along Oakhurst Road at the driveway.

The Board made the following findings for Use Special Permit:

1. The appropriateness of the specific site as a location for the use; The Board finds the specific site is appropriate for the proposed contracting use because the site is zoned for the use. Additionally, information provided shows a minimal effect on the neighborhood.
2. The adequacy of sewerage and water systems; The Board finds there is adequate provisions for wastewater treatment and water supply.
3. The effect of the developed use upon the neighborhood; The Board finds the effect of the use upon the neighborhood will be minimal.
4. Whether there will be undue nuisance or serious hazard to vehicles or pedestrians; and, The Board finds there will be no undue nuisance or serious hazard to vehicles or pedestrians.
5. Whether adequate and appropriate facilities will be provided to ensure the proper operation of the proposed use, structure, or condition. The Board finds adequate and appropriate facilities will be provided to ensure the proper operation of the proposed use, structure, or condition as demonstrated through thorough review of the site plans by the Town's peer review engineers and departments who have no outstanding concerns.

Motion: To grant the Special Permit for Akiles Realty Associate for the use of 24 Oakhurst Road as a contractors site in accordance with the Table of Use Regulations – Section G.3. landscape contractor and G.8. Other contractor, not including paving, as well as Site Plan Approval, and a Class 2 Earth Disturbance & Removal Permit based on record plans dated 7/22/26 & 7/27/26 and subject to the following conditions: R. Largess Jr.

**Prior to Commencement of Construction:**

1. Within sixty (60) days, the applicant shall provide a final set of plans with any waivers granted and conditions of approval on the plan set for the Board's endorsement as the record set of plans upon which construction shall be based.
2. All required approvals and/or permits shall be received from applicable permitting authorities, especially the Fire Department.

**During Construction:**

3. Unless a specific exception is approved by the Planning Director or Building Commissioner, construction shall be limited to Monday through Friday, 7:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. and Saturdays, 8:00 a.m. to 12:00 p.m., and shall exclude Sundays and the following holidays: New Year's Day, Memorial Day, Independence Day, Labor Day, Thanksgiving, after 12 PM on Christmas Eve, and Christmas. From November 15th to April 1st equipment may be started at 6:30 a.m. but no construction may commence until 7:00 a.m. unless a specific exception is granted as noted above.
4. The Applicant shall maintain all feasible and reasonable means of dust control and shall collect all trash and debris daily.
5. The Applicant shall implement measures to ensure that noise during construction activities does not exceed acceptable levels, as set forth by Federal and State regulatory agencies. The Applicant shall cease any excessively loud noise during construction activities when directed by a duly appointed agent of the Board. No excessively loud activities are permitted prior to 8:00 AM or after 5:00 PM.

**Prior to Issuance of Building or Sign Permits:**

6. Prior to issuance of permits for signage at the site, the applicant shall submit a compliant sign design and receive approval from the Planning Board.

**Prior to Issuance of Occupancy Permits:**

7. Prior to issuance of a certificate of occupancy on any building, the Applicant shall submit to the Planning Board and receive approval for an As-Built Plan and written certification from the Project's engineer that the site and all infrastructure to serve this area of the site has been constructed substantially in accordance with the Site Plan. Additionally, the Applicant shall provide an As-Built plan to the Town of Sutton Assessors in accordance with their requirements.
8. Prior to issuance of occupancy on any structure a knox box with building access keys and/or codes, a building layout plan and emergency contact shall be installed to the satisfaction of the Fire Department.

**Ongoing Site Maintenance & Operations:**

9. The Applicant shall ensure proper maintenance of plantings on the site, including immediate replacement of dead or diseased plantings unless it is winter or summer, in which case in the following planting season.
10. The applicant shall comply with the final O&M plan for the site drainage systems. Inspection and maintenance shall be performed in accordance with the recommended schedule and an inspection form shall be prepared by the inspector, including any required correction actions to be taken. Any required correction actions shall be promptly implemented by the owner at its expense. Copies of all inspection shall be submitted to the Planning Dept annually.
11. The Board reserves the right to review lighting and require adjustments if they find it to be a danger or nuisance.
12. The Board reserves the right to review and assess noise or other complaints related to onsite operations. If the applicant/operator fails to cure or remedy a complaint the Board deems to be valid within a reasonable time as determined by the Board, the Board reserves the right to require the applicant and/or operator to provide adequate mitigation.
13. Prior to signing a lease with any future tenants, the tenants or owner will provide detailed information about their operation to the Planning Department and will acquire any additional approvals deemed necessary.

2nd: E. McCallum

Vote: 5-0-0, E. McCallum- aye, R Largess Jr. – aye, M. Gagan – aye, W. Stanhope – aye, D. Mason – aye

2nd: E. McCallum

### 1R Lackey Dam Road (40 Lackey Dam in Uxbridge) – Blackstone Logistics – tenant space adjustment

Elizabeth Clark of Tighe & Bond and Michael Tague of Channel Building Company were present to request waiver of Site Plan Review for the adjustments the property owner would like to make to the parking and building at 1R Lackey Dam Road that were reviewed at the last meeting. Approximately 2,580 s.f. will be converted to office space with the balance of the tenant space containing a separate 150 s.f. electrical/utility room and approximately 160k s.f. open warehouse space. Five large windows will be added along the north and west building sides of the northwest building corner. As existing employee parking is over ¼ mile away, sixteen (16) new parking spaces are proposed including 8 against the building and 8 to be converted from nearby truck to car parking. A tracking diagram was also provided showing that tractor trailers can navigate the site with the new parking. Clearance behind the building facing spaces will be 27'.

Motion: To waive Site Plan review and allow interior and façade renovations for the structure at 1R Lackey Dam Road for a 2,580 s.f. office and 150 s.f. utility room, addition of 8 parking spaces and conversion of 8 truck to car parking spaces for a potential tenant as shown on the record plans dated 6/3/26 – 7/21/26 conditioned on the approval of all other applicable permitting authorities and reinforcement of condition #18 from the original use special permit requiring that once a building occupant and/or subsequent tenant(s) are known, a written statement of the proposed user and their operational characteristics shall be submitted to the Planning Board. In the event that the characteristics demonstrates additional truck or employee parking is necessary, an amended Site Plan shall be submitted and approved and this parking and any related landscaping shall be constructed prior to this tenants' occupancy. W. Stanhope

2nd: R. Largess Jr.

Vote: 5-0-0, E. McCallum- aye, R Largess Jr. – aye, M. Gagan – aye, W. Stanhope – aye, D. Mason – aye

(D. Mason stepped down from the Board due to potential conflict as he sometimes works with C. Windle)

### 26R Oakhurst Road – Alternate access determination

Land owner Chris Windle of 6 Old County Road and Raouf Mankaryous, P.E. of Alpha Omega Engineering, Sutton, were present to hear the input of Town Counsel and receive the Board determination on a requested footnote 12 alternate access determination. The status of legal frontage for this lot is the key issue. Correspondence provided by Mr. Windle at the last meeting including their updated reasoning why the Board can and should grant this finding and a 1979 Plan that showed the lot in its existing configuration with a cart road for access out to Oakhurst Road was provided to Town Counsel. As is the standard protocol in this type of request for guidance, Town Counsel provided a response to/spoke with the Community Development Director to convey his input. She stated that while the argument provided had logic to it, the first hurdle of the requested finding, that the lot in question have legal frontage, has not been cleared in the opinion of Town Counsel. He does not agree the lot has legal frontage. While most in attendance agreed it would be beneficial to take a low value piece of land and create a business, jobs and taxable buildings/assets, the Board did not see this as justification to deviate from the input of Counsel.

Motion: The Board declines to make a footnote 12 finding based on input of Town Counsel that this lot does not appear to have legal frontage which is required to proceed with an alternate access finding, W. Stanhope

2nd: R. Largess Jr.

Vote: 4-0-0, E. McCallum- aye, R Largess Jr. – aye, M. Gagan – aye, W. Stanhope – aye
